Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 109, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Kafirun (The Disbelievers), because the word "al-Kafirun" occurs at its beginning.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• To make clear the separation and distinction between the worship of Allah and the worship of others, that the two cannot be combined, that the religion of Islam does not mix with anything of the religion of polytheism, and to make the polytheists despair of the Messenger (ﷺ) ever agreeing with them in any part of the disbelief they are upon.

[The Tafsir]

Say, O Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: "O you disbelievers in Allah!"
I do not worship what you worship of idols and false deities.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 109, verse 3:

Nor are you worshipping what I worship, [namely] the one God, the Lord of the worlds, who alone deserves to be worshipped.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 109, verse 4:

"And I will not be worshipping what you worship, [of] the idols and the false deities."
And you will not worship what I worship, now or in the future. This verse was revealed about particular individuals among the polytheists whom God knew would never believe.
For you is your religion, which you have insisted on following, and for me is my religion, which I do not seek anything other than.
